utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey, you intimated that you would ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. President. We have managed to sort out my problem with the -- with the log and so I think if I can just go back to one log we should finish up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if I could get the help of the usher, to give the witness two original logs that they will help him take a look because I'm not sure you were able to see all of this before because we may have been missing one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stanisic. The log we talked about yesterday was for a TAM 80 and that was Prosecution's 303 and that -- I've also given you a log for a TAM 75, which is Prosecution 945. Now, the yellow sticky, the one with the yellow sticky on it is the new one, the TAM 75. If you could take a look at that one, the originals are right next to you so you can look at it there as well. It might be easier for you. And if you could hand him both, just so he can compare the two to see -- to confirm that we are talking about two different trucks here. First of all, are we talking about two different trucks? Do each of those two logs have to do with two different trucks?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's look at this new log, the one that's got the yellow sticky that's at this thing next to you that we call the ELMO. If we look at the page that's on the ELMO now, it's hard to make out, but it has the same two drivers on it, Dragomir Topalovic and Vlado Josic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To be clear, is this 945?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, the one that we are seeing on the ELMO is 945, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the difference is between a TAM 75 and a TAM 80?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Believe me, they are the same for me. The bearing capacity is the same, two and a half tonnes. They have a wooden bed with a tarpaulin. If I understood your question well. You're asking me about the difference between these two trucks, in terms of their - how shall I put it - purpose and characteristics. They are the same to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And maybe we -- if we can put 945 on the e-court too you may get a better look at it, the reflection from Mr. ELMO is not good. All right. Now, let's take 945, the one on the ELMO and turn it over so we can see the actual route section that gives the indication where the vehicle went, so if you can just turn that over? And this is page 2 of the B/C/S on e-court and page 2 of the English. Now, if we again go, focus our attention on 15 July on this particular truck, again we see, "Petkovci-Brana-Petkovci", number of journeys, four. People, 1 plus 8. Now, can you explain this entry?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to this, there were four journeys, and one plus eight probably means that there was a driver plus eight troops or any eight people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know if those eight people were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know if those people were alive or dead?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wouldn't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that should finish that exhibit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I note Mr. Ostojic is not here today but Mr. Meek, you will continue your cross-examination or you're done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, thank you after consulting with the client we have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Zivanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So Mr. Zivanovic is representing Mr. Popovic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I only have a couple questions for you. As I was reading the interview you provided on the second occasion in March 2002, as far as I can remember, I've noticed that the investigator informed you that he wanted to copy a personal note, the notes that you had in front of you while you were talking to him. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understood from your position, you were against those notes being copied?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I've also noticed that he told you that he would certainly do it despite your protestations because those were his authorities from the Tribunal. My question to you is this: Did he ever show you such an authority?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Once he copied your personal notes, the investigator told you that the copying of those notes would protect you. Did he maybe explain to you how the copying would serve to protect your interests?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that conversation. I don't remember that he ever mentioned the word "protect." He only told me that the documents were something that he needed, that he had a right to take the notebook from me and to copy it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... If we're going to be getting into the detail of what the investigator's saying and what he remembers, it would be fair to have the witness see his answers and the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown the exhibit and the passage I was referring to is on page 80.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The investigator says literally, and I'm reading from --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: What is the exhibit number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please bear with me. 7D266. Page 80 in the B/C/S version, and page 78 in English, I believe, but just let me double-check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could check the page in front of you is the right page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Just a moment, please. Bear with me. I was looking at another text, which is only in B/C/S, and what I have in front of me is a combination of both languages. So I don't have that. I am not in a position to give you the exact number since the text that we were originally given has been changed. First we were given a combined B/C/S-English version and later on we were provided with two separate versions, and I can only refer the number of page in the B/C/S version, and I can also ask the usher to place the text on the ELMO, or I can read it verbatim. I am sorry, I apologise, I'm not in a position to give you the exact number of the page in this particular version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We can --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 3D149. Could I please call up that document? Page 80. In the English version, this is on page 72.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So Mr. Stanisic, do you have that passage in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you scroll down a little, please? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the initials DM and when DM is mentioned for the third time from the bottom, and it says here, "One of the reasons for which I would like to photocopy your notes is the fact that this may protect you." It's on page 74 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The very beginning. Since I do not see any explanation that was provided to you or at least it has not been recorded in the transcript, I'm asking you if the investigator maybe explained to you how the photocopying of your personal notes might protect you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. He did not give me any explanations, and believe me, I really could not remember this passage when you first asked me about it. I can see it now but he never explained anything to me. He didn't tell me why he would need the notes and how I would be protected by those notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: He kept your notes?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Did he maybe explain to you how he would protect you if he kept your notes?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: The entire interview between the investigator and yourself, was it recorded on a tape?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know why I'm asking you this? In one part of that conversation, the investigator says to you that he is giving you back your ID, your personal ID. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I can locate that in the document to jog your memory. I'm asking you this because nowhere in the interview did I see a reference made to him taking the ID from you. I conclude from that that the ID was taken from you before the beginning of the interview. Can you remember that detail?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. Why my ID was taken, whether it was taken at the beginning or when, I really can't remember anything about the ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You can look at page 83 of your interview. He says here, "Here, this is your ID. I'm giving it back to you."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. [Interpretation] Just a moment, Your Honours, please. Bear with me. I'm sorry, I'm not in a position to give you the number. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's get on with the B/C/S version for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: So you don't remember this particular detail?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't remember him giving the ID to me but he did give me back my notebook.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: One more question. Did you maybe keep the invitation to that interview?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I have it at home but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether, in that invitation, it says that whatever personal effects you might bring might be taken away from you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any more questions for this witness, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. Who will go next? Madam Nikolic. Madam Nikolic is representing Mr. Drago Nikolic. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stanisic. I will start off with a few clarifications of your previous testimony. Yesterday on page 11623 of the transcript, and even before, when asked a question by my colleague from the Prosecution concerning the guarding of prisoners in the school in Petkovci, you said the prisoners had come with soldiers who were guarding them already and your battalion did not need to participate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You did not go to that school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And you know -- and you don't know from which unit those soldier-guards were?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but my deputy supposed, since they had white belts, that they could be from military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Madam Nikolic, just to bear in mind that you should put a pause between question and answer for the sake of interpreters, please. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I will take care.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Let's slow down, both of us. Thank you, Mr. Stanisic. But your deputy did not tell you from which unit that military police was and he didn't know that, did he?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I would like to discuss with you the location of the school. You showed yesterday, and during proofing, you determined the position of the old school and the new school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And the distance between them was 600 to 800 metres, correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: The new school is removed from the road that goes from Petkovci, from the new school to the old school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: According to this aerial photograph, the new school is removed from that road, the main road, that leads to Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: There is a field between them, between the road and the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I'll show you that aerial photograph again, unmarked, so maybe we can more easily determine where that plateau was that was cleared later.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have in e-court 1352, please? Sorry, 3D152. Could we zoom in a little? Further up, please. That's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I think now, if I'm not mistaken, we can see the new school.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: That's the building to the left on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell us, relative to that building, where is the plateau, before the school looking from the road or behind the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's on the left, this smaller white surface above the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Could you please take that pen -- could the usher please give a pen to the witness to show us where the plateau is?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we turn this picture to make it easier for the witness by 45 degrees to the right? 90 degrees, my colleague corrects me, 90 degrees to the right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just to ignore this marking for the moment. Yes, we can do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could we go down a little? Sorry. Could we see a little further up, just to see the school building? I think this is all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, is it now clear to you that this is the same photograph, the same building, or are you now confused?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can see it, it's the same photograph. But I put the marking a little further up than necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: I will now ask you to make a circle around the same plateau.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Put the letter "P" for plateau.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And the date in the right, bottom corner, with your initials.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And just another question regarding this photograph. From the main road, since the facade of the school faces the road, the front side faces the road, can you see the plateau from the road?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And I thank the usher for her assistance. Now, I would like to ask you about the time that your assistant commander -- I think we can remove this exhibit now. You were asked yesterday about the time that Mr. Marko Milosevic spent in meeting with Beara and Nikolic at Petkovci. From what I understood from your testimony, Milosevic didn't go to a meeting, he just went to convey a message?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Because he didn't know who would be at the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you were talking yesterday about the visit to the brigade command on the invitation that you received on the 14th of July, that's page 11598 of the transcript, you said you departed for the brigade around 11.00, together with your soldiers?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said between 11.00 and 12.00, I departed for the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You mean the brigade command in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Do you remember when you arrived, approximately?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been 12.00, between 12.00 and 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And there, you met with the duty operations officer?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you meet with any other officer of the Zvornik Brigade at that command?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you know Drago Nikolic, assistant Chief of Staff or rather assistant commander for security?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you see Drago Nikolic on that day, on the 14th of July, at the building called Standard?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Did you see or hear from Drago Nikolic during those days?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Neither.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just lets confirm whether the witness actually said no when asked whether he knew Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He said yes, if I'm not mistaken. I'm sorry, I didn't see this.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, did you know Drago Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: And to my last question, when I asked you if you had seen or heard from Drago Nikolic during those days, your answer was --

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: You said, "I neither saw nor heard from Drago Nikolic."

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I neither heard nor -- from nor saw Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Madam Fauveau? She is representing General Miletic. Please go ahead, Madam Fauveau-Ivanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you spoke about that discussion you had with Dragan Obrenovic before the first time you were interviewed by the OTP. I would like to know about this conversation with Dragan Obrenovic. It was not spontaneous. You were invited by Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the then-commander, Dragan Obrenovic, invited me to his office to talk. I didn't know what it was all about.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when you say Commander Dragan Obrenovic, at that time Dragan Obrenovic was in the same brigade as you, he was commander of the brigade where you were an officer, a superior officer?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, I was battalion commander and he was brigade commander, and he was free to invite me or summon me at any time to discuss whatever he required, in view of my duties. I didn't know why he was inviting me to talk on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And in fact, during that talk, Dragan Obrenovic suggested to you that you shouldn't reveal certain things during the interview you were going to have with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, since I was about to go to Banja Luka to have that interview, he was aware of that, and we were just talking because he had already been there once or twice, I can't remember any more, and quite simply I asked him what it all looked like, what things are discussed, what the relationship is, but when I asked him whether -- what to say if they asked me whether there had been any cleaning up of the school and the plateau, he said that it is not advisable and that's what I said yesterday in my testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Really, since he was your superior commander, you followed his instructions during your interview with the investigators of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I would like to ask you a couple of questions concerning the 14th of July 1995. If I understood correctly, you were aware that the prisoners were going to arrive at Petkovci in the afternoon of the 14th.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found out about those prisoners in the afternoon, not before.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you did hear the shooting in the afternoon of the 14th, you heard the shots?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But you did not go to see what had happened?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because my deputy informed me that he had been notified of the impending arrival of the prisoners to the school, that they would be accommodated at the school, that no security is required, so I didn't need to go to the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you go after the departure of the prisoners to that school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime later, I did go to the school, but maybe 10 days later, because we used the plateau for our own leisure activities. There was a football pitch there and whenever we had some spare time, we came there for recreation.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember if you were able to see when you entered the school any traces of gunfire on the walls of the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't go inside the school because it was locked up.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct that that school had previously been used in 1992 and 1993 to accommodate certain military units?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know in which period it was, but for a while sabotage and reconnaissance units were put up there but I can't remember if it was before or after.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Could we show to the witness 5D302?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm sorry, we haven't yet received the translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, can you confirm that it is an order from the Zvornik Brigade command dated 14 September 1993?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And for the benefit of the people who do not speak B/C/S, could you read paragraph 2 of this order?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I order... " You mean this.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Yes, but only what is written after number 2. It's the second paragraph, what follows after number 2.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The trainee unit to be accommodated in the area of Petkovci village in the building of the primary school and while training is to be carried out in the broader area of Petkovci villages and Klisa -- Petkovci and Klisa villages."

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Does this refresh your memory, namely that sometimes military units were put up at that school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the duration of my stay there, the 6th Battalion was established. In 1993, I was not at Petkovci. I was further away, in Memici or at Malasic so that in 1993, I did not serve in Petkovci at all as a commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you remember that indeed you spoke in your interview of year 2000 of the fact that sometimes military units were put up at that school, that the soldiers consumed a lot of alcohol and shooting incidents occurred sometimes? It's page 38 in the interview of year 2000.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I recall that. When it was necessary to go out into the field somewhere, then the unit that was supposed to go would assemble and on those occasions they would be put up at the school. But that was as part of the preparations for departure into the field, into one of the locations.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Well, that's all that I was asking. And in fact, you can confirm today as well that sometimes shooting occurred, shooting incidents occurred, when those troops were in the school building?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You said yesterday that in 1995, in July 1995, that belonged to the civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that in July 1995, in the territory that you call the free territory, where there was no combat, civilian authorities operated normally?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge, they functioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And when you received the message that villagers were requiring a truck in order to clean out the school, did those villagers ask just for a truck or did they want somebody from the brigade -- sorry, somebody from the battalion, to help clean up?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As from that call from the communications centre of the battalion, it was about the villagers who had come to ask for a truck to clean up the plateau of the school, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know if the civilian authorities, the authorities who were in charge of that school at Petkovci, had been consulted before the prisoners were placed inside the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As battalion commander, it was not my responsibility to deal with such matters. It would be the military department. If a school or any other facility needed to be requisitioned for the needs of the army, a request would need to be submitted and then the authorities would either approve or not approve that this facility be given for the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And while the prisoners were in the school, you did not receive any calls from the civilian authorities asking you what had happened at the school, who was at the school, or anything of that kind?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not receive any calls from them.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct that one of your responsibilities was to report to your brigade, to your superior command?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you know that the brigade would then forward combat reports to its own superior command, namely the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you were also aware that combat brigades [as interpreted] sent by the brigade had to precisely reflect the situation on the ground?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: In fact, you, people like you, people at battalion level, had to draft the reports to the brigade so that the brigade could inform the corps of the situation on the ground exactly as it was?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But as for the area of defence of my battalion and combat readiness within my battalion. That was the subject of my reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'd like to point out for record, line 4 of page 18, which reads "combat brigade" should be reading as "combat reports." Thank you, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it correct that you did not send your report to the brigade to inform them that the prisoners had arrived to the school in Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not send that report for the simple reason that the brigade was the one that informed me of the impending arrival of the prisoners, so I didn't send that report.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And you didn't inform the brigade of the shooting in Petkovci either?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And after you learned of the presence of certain bodies around the school, you did not inform the brigade of that either?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That's a misstatement of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If the Prosecutor means the question, I don't see any misstatement. Where is the misstatement? Where is the statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He testified that he informed his commander at the time on the -- I believe it was the 15th, Obrenovic, about the bodies. It's my view that a question cannot misstate the evidence to such a degree. It misleads the witness, it misleads the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In light of Mr. McCloskey's intervention, could you reformulate your question again?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will show this witness a number of documents. I believe this will be a simpler course to follow. Can we show the witness P326?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, this is a regular combat report issued by the Zvornik Brigade that was drafted on the 14th of July 1995. I would like you to read this report, which only has one page, and after having done that, can you please tell me whether there is a reference in this document to the prisoners in Petkovci? Can we scroll down, please, so that the witness can see the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Is it true that there is no reference in this document to the prisoners in Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we now show to the witness Exhibit P327? This is not an extremely good copy. However, I hope you will still be able to read it. Can you see at the beginning, although it is not very clear, that this is an interim report issued by the Zvornik Brigade on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: At the bottom of the document, can we please show the seal and according to the seal on the document, it arises that the document was dispatched on the 15th July 1995, at 0110 hours.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And now could you please make an effort and try and read the entire text? Can we now place the entire text on the screen for the witness? And after that I'm going to ask you whether this report was sent between 14 and 15 July, and whether it contains any reference to the prisoners in Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we enlarge the letters a bit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Give it a try. Now, can you read now? We enlarged a little bit. Could you take a look?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try. I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, maybe a hard copy would be easier for the witness to read.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Tonight around 2020 hours in the general sector of Maricici, a large group of Muslims passed through and continued towards the Zvornik-Caparde road. The column, which was between 2 and 3 kilometres long --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Stanisic, you are not required to read aloud all the entire text. What you were asked for is that whether, after reading it, if you could answer whether this report was sent between 14 and 15th July and whether it contains any reference to the prisoners in Petkovci.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I've read the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- In Petkovci? Sir, can you confirm that this document does not make a reference to the prisoners in Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we now show to the witness Exhibit P328? Sir, can you see that this is another regular combat report issued on the 15th of July 1995 by the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: One more time, I will kindly ask you to read this document, which is a bit longer than a page, and once again confirm for me that no reference is made to the prisoners in Petkovci in this document. Could you please inform us when you're finished the reading of the part that is on the screen so that we could lower the page?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While he's reading this, I don't take it that the Prosecution is challenging this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, we'll stipulate that it's not there, Your Honour. I don't know why he has to read this.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does it mean that the Prosecutor agrees that the Zvornik Brigade did not inform the Drina Corps about the prisoners in Petkovci and the killings that took place around the school in Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, Mr. President, I don't have any other option.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the page be lowered, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the rest of the document to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please move on. Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, have you been able to find a reference to the prisoners in the document anywhere?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The prisoners are not mentioned anywhere in this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we now show the witness Exhibit P329?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau, to the same effect?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the Prosecution agrees that there is no mention, no reference to the prisoners or bodies in Petkovci, I don't think there is any point to ask the witness to read the whole document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This next document is a bit more interesting, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Let's see that. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I absolutely agree with my learned friend in that respect.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Sir, this is a document which was issued on the 15th of July 1995. This is another interim combat report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we scroll down just a little bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This document, Your Honour, I would think we should give the witness a chance to read the whole document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in this document, a reference is made to the prisoners and in order to avoid wasting time, I would like to show the witness particularly the part where prisoners are mentioned, but if my learned friend insists on the witness reading the entire document, I will not object to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I do object to the -- to informing the witness of her -- the theory of her case or her cross-examination, but the first part of the document talks about his -- the combat situation, his battalion. I think to put the context of this, that he ought to be able to read the whole thing. It's very short.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I would agree. This is not very long; I would allow the witness to read through this document. Let's scroll up a little bit so that he can follow, from the first -- from the first part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you scroll up or scroll down?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the rest of the document, if there is more?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show the rest of the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: You could see that this document speaks of the prisoners who were in the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And it shows the concern of the brigade command about the safety issues in the region of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: But not for a single moment does the document speak of the shots or the murder or killing of the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we now show to the witness Exhibit P330? Sir, this was issued on the 16th of July 1995. It is a regular combat report issued by the Zvornik Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we see, at the very bottom of the document, where you can see the seal, the stamp? Can you see that this document was dispatched on 16 July at 1810 hours; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And on the 16th of July, in the morning, you had your conversation with Dragan Obrenovic, is that true?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can you please look at the document and tell me whether a reference is made in this document to the prisoners in the Petkovci school. Can we please show the beginning of the document, the beginning of the text, to the witness?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we show the rest of the document, please? Can we show the rest of the document to the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Go on, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I believe that this is the end. Is it true that the document which was sent at 1810, after your conversation with Dragan Obrenovic, does not mention the prisoners in Petkovci and the developments that took place in Petkovci on the 14th and 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we show paragraph 1 of this document? In paragraph 1 of this document, of this report, there is a reference to a Muslim attack at positions held, among others, by your battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And indeed, during those days, you sustained attacks from the Muslim side and you had losses, soldiers were wounded and killed?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we show 5D303 to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, we haven't yet received the translation for this document and, on top of that, the copy is very bad.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, do you have before you an order to attack, issued by the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the command of the 245th Mountain Brigade, dated 13th July 1995?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we show the bottom of this page, paragraph 2? Could you please read this paragraph, the one that begins with "units belonging to the 28th Division"? Could you please read it aloud?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Units of the 28th Division of ground forces decided to break out from the circle, from the encirclement, through enemy lines along the following axis, column: Srebrenica, Konjevic Polje, Cerska, Kamenica, Crni Vrh, Baljkovica, and Crni Vrh, Sprecanska Dolina and along the axis --"

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: This is enough for me. Is it true that the areas you just mentioned, this axis of movement of the 28th Division, was in the vicinity of your battalion?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Crni Vrh was the closest to the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Can we now show this witness page 3? I hope that you are going to be able to see a little better, paragraph 5, top of the page. These are tasks assigned to this unit of the BH army, to commence an attack as specified in this paragraph, along the axis specified in the paragraph.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Part of this attack was against your forces, correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Baljkovica, Tisova Kosa and Nezuk Parlog.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Just a moment ago, you answered a couple of questions concerning that logbook, that diary you had and that the investigator took from you during your interview in 2002. What I would like to know is this: Do you know that at the time you said that this diary was not relevant to this case, with the exception of the end of that diary, which you discussed with the investigator of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This diary was my preparation. After the first interview I made certain notes to remind myself of what I said during the first interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And the representatives of the OTP copied that part as well?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They copied the set, all of my notes, and gave me a copy to separate what is not relevant to them. But I said, "You've already copied it all. You can keep it all." That's at least what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: I wanted to show you your diary so that you can show us which part is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't know if it would be more judicious to give a hard copy to the witness so he can review it during the break so we don't waste any more time because the break is in three minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We would agree unless the Prosecution object to that idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. I think that's a good idea and we've got a copy so that would facilitate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Shall we take a break now?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, and after the break, I would have just a few questions about the diary and would finish soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll break for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Fauveau-Ivanovic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Witness, did you have occasion to see a copy of your journal, of your diary?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Did you find the part relevant to the discussion you had with the OTP?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is a mistake here. This is not the diary that was taken from me during the interview.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I must ask you to urge the OTP to let us have the copy of the diary that was taken from the witness during the interview and that contains the part relevant to this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Personal note, do you have it with you, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We had endeavoured to find all that. We thought that was the one we were talking about. We'll see if there is something else. This is the original that we believed was connected to this interview. Sometimes these things get confused but perhaps the witness can help us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let the witness take a look at it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is not the diary. There is another diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could ask, is this your diary, that one I just gave you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It's my diary, but it was a smaller agenda book. What I have here was a military booklet that was in common use in the army. And that's what I used in the army in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: As far as I recall, there is one mention of one diary, and this is the diary that we have that's connected to this interview and it is his diary. So we'll continue to look but there may be a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Maybe the witness is confused. Perhaps we're confused. But I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the witness has been confused on this but can we explore whether we can pursue this issue without seeing the actual agenda or what would you recommend?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked a couple of questions concerning this diary of the witness, precisely in order to find out where the relevant passage is because I was unable to find it myself and now I understand why. I don't know whether the witness can clarify any further. But it's clear from his testimony today, and from his interview with the Prosecution in 2002, that there was a diary or a notebook containing several pages relevant to the interview the witness had with the investigator of the OTP in 2002. Maybe the investigator could provide more clarification when he comes to testify because he's on the witness list. We will take it up with him. But in any case I'm convinced that there is another notebook because that is abundantly clear from the interview of this witness with the OTP and I wanted to ask for these pages to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And apart from that issue, you're done?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, Mr. President. I'm sorry. I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is only one notebook that we copied. This is the notebook we copied from the interview. And that's the situation. I will, of course, look into the possibility of a second notebook but I don't believe there is any suggestion of a second notebook but I will, of course, look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please take a look again. And let's leave that matter there and shall we proceed? I take it Defence for Mr. Borovcanin will ask some questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, indeed we did ask for 15 minutes to cross-examine the witness but after we heard his testimony we decided not to cross-examine him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And my understanding is that General Gvero's team is not minded to ask any question.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Your understanding is correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about Mr. Pandurevic's Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, we are going to ask this witness some questions, probably for about half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stanisic, how are you?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: As you've heard me say, I've probably got about half an hour's worth of questions for you so you're coming near to the end of your ordeal you'll be pleased to hear. And I want to start by showing you some documents on the computer screen which I'm going to ask you, with the aid of the lady usher, to mark for us. So can we start please by putting into e-court 3D94? And I wonder whether Mr. Stanisic could be shown how to use the pen to mark this document. Take a little time, Mr. Stanisic, to orient yourself on that map but is that area familiar to you? You should see in the top right-hand corner Klisa and then coming across, Nezuk, Baljkovica, Delici, roughly the area in which your battalion operated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what I'd like you to do, if you could take up a pen, which you'll be provided with now, is to mark firstly on that map the defence line of the 6th Battalion. Before you mark it, can we just move the map slightly to the left so that it includes Petkovci? A little more. Just a touch more. That's perfect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, rub it out and correct it.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to mark the 6th Infantry Battalion. Is that necessary?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like you to put "6 PB" there, please, if you would.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And while you're there, would you mark, as best you can, the line of the battalion whose defence line was immediately to the left of yours, and, again, put the number and the name of that battalion?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it's impossible for you to mark it but can you just tell us the number and the name of the battalion which had a defence line to the right of yours?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 2nd Infantry Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now would you just mark in relation to your battalion where your forward command post was?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would you write under that "IKM"?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And your rear units, please, if you could mark them on?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just put "RU" there, please, if you would.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And lastly, they are obvious on the map, but would you just locate for us where the battalion command was in Petkovci, as best you can?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we can -- I mean, would you put "KM" there, please?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. "KM"?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And lastly, I believe that in Klisa, there was some brigade artillery units. Would you mark as best you can on the map where they would be and put appropriate initials there?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He is agreeing that there is an artillery unit there? It's not clear from the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you agree that there were brigade artillery units in Klisa? That's a question for you, Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, since you agree that, would you, as best you can, make a mark to indicate where they were?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Maybe a bit of map is missing. Maybe they were further up but they were at the forward post. They occupied the highest elevation at Klisa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Would you just put under the mark you've made "BAU", brigade artillery units? And then we are finished with marking this map.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the bottom right-hand corner, would you just put "OS" for Ostoja Stanisic and put today's date, which I think is the 17th of May.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if that could be preserved, please? And could we next have in e-court, please, P2815? Perfect. Thank you very much. I wonder whether Mr. Stanisic could be provided, please, with a pen in blue, for example, a colour different to that in which the map is already marked. What I'd like you to do for me, if you can, here, Mr. Stanisic, is firstly indicate in blue on the map the road into Petkovci from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you continue that route as if you were driving all the way up and into the back of the school where the plateau is?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. Do you want me to go to the crossroads or do you want me to go even beyond the crossroads?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, it looks to me from this image as if the route into the school would involve you turning right up the right-hand side of the school and going into the back of it. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I didn't quite understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, at the crossroads, which way would you go to get to the back of the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You want me to draw that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If you would, that would be very kind.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And at the far right-hand end of that blue line that you've drawn, would you just put an arrow and write underneath it "Zvornik"?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Excellent. Now I'd like you, if you would, to show us the direction a vehicle would travel to go to the dam at Petkovci from the school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to draw a new line next to the one that I have already drawn on the map?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you use a different colour?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, it's probably simpler, if it means going in the same direction, namely towards Zvornik, if he writes "dam" underneath the line as well and another arrow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just before we leave this, looking at the new school, which is marked with a "2" on the existing plan, we can see certain buildings all around it, quite a number to the right and the left. They are all houses, are they?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder if you'd mind just circling two or three of them and writing "houses" underneath that.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, if you wouldn't mind, I'd suggest, in the bottom left-hand corner this time, again putting your initials and today's date on that item.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. 17th today?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Unless it's changed in the last ten minutes, yes.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I'd just like to clarify a few things you've said over the course of the last two days. Do I understand you correctly to say that a battalion, according to your understanding of military law, had no zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The battalion had a defence sector, whereas when you say the area of responsibility, you mean a brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And just briefly, in words, would you describe what you regarded to be the defence sector of the 6th Battalion?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say a defence sector, I mean a defence line and customarily on the right-hand side a point is marked where that line starts and along that line, several points are marked which are typical of that line, and then on the left flank, another point is determined, be it a river, a facility, and then the sector is also defined in depth and this is usually 2.5 to 3 kilometres. Then places are defined and in my case this was Kitovnica and Grbavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And so to clear that up, your understanding of your responsibility was that you had to defend a line and an area 2 and a half to three kilometres deep from that line; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not fully understand what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That's probably because it was a bad question. I'm going to move on. Was it your understanding that you had any responsibility for what went on in civil buildings in Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have any responsibility whatsoever for these civilian facilities. As a commander, my duty was to be on the defence line, i.e. at the forward command post. More specifically, my duty was to look after the combat readiness of my battalion. Also, in case of attack, it was my duty to defend and protect my positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you described for us briefly yesterday the procedure by which a unit of the army could mobilise or requisition a building such as the school. So far as you were aware, was that done in relation to the Petkovci school, by either your battalion or your brigade?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the school in Petkovci, I don't know whether it had been requisitioned. As a commander of that battalion, I did not need the school, and it was not requisitioned for my battalion. I never requested the school to be requisitioned for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were asked some questions a little while ago about the use of the school in 1993 as a training facility. In 1995, had your battalion ever made use of the new school at Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we come, please, to the 14th of July? On the 14th of July, you took some men to brigade command for use by Dragan Obrenovic in the Snagovo region; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: How long were you at brigade command in dropping off those men?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember exactly when they returned. I believe that they had been away from the battalion a couple of days.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sorry, probably my fault, you misunderstood my question. I wanted to know how long you were at brigade command on the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe an hour or up to an hour, if you're asking me about the time, it was not longer than 60 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you speak to the duty officer?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just handed my troops over. I lined them up, I handed them over. At that moment, my duties were over and done with. From there, I returned to my defence positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And about what time of day was that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that. It may have been between 12.00 and 1.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And while you were there, did anybody make any mention of prisoners being brought to Petkovci?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody mentioned prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: As I understand it, the first you knew about that was a telephone call you received once you had arrived back in Petkovci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned that from my deputy, Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how long was that after you'd arrived back?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I arrived in Petkovci around 1700 hours. If I was at Standard up until 1300, I returned to my defence positions maybe three or four hours after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you learn from Milosevic at what time he'd received the call?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't very specific about the time. He only informed me that he had been informed about some prisoners being brought to the school. He did not mention the time, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at that time, the Zvornik Brigade was under the command of Dragan Obrenovic, who was a major; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you know that the commander of the Zvornik Brigade, Vinko Pandurevic, was a lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just a moment. Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. I said did you know that the commander of the Zvornik Brigade at the time was Vinko Pandurevic, who was a lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was a brigade commander, and his deputy was chief Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, that afternoon, Milosevic received a call which contained a message for a colonel; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I received the call, and I sent Milosevic to convey the message to whomever was necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The point I'm making is yesterday you told us, and it's page 23, line 13, that the message was for a Colonel Beara. That's right, isn't it? You knew the message was for a colonel?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So that was necessarily a message for a man of a higher rank than anybody in the Zvornik Brigade; that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that message was related to prisoners at the Petkovci school, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The message was, "Inform Colonel Beara."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did Milosevic have to go to deliver that message?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was supposed to go to the new school, or somewhere around the new school. I was told that Colonel Beara is supposed to be somewhere around there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've already told us that your battalion had nothing to do with guarding these prisoners or anything to do with what was going on at the Petkovci school. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when you discovered, following the first message relating to the expected arrival of prisoners, and then the second message to deliver a message to a colonel at the new school, did you deduce that this had nothing to do with the brigade either?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Tell me, what right, power or authority did you have to stop a colonel from carrying out any sort of activity at the Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection, vague, "any sort of activity", I think we can -- it doesn't have a lot of relevance when it's that vaguely described.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'll rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What right did you have to interfere with the actions of a colonel at the Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a battalion commander, I was responsible for my unit. If any higher officers from a higher command arrived, they could command me, they could take over the battalion, they could issue orders and I can only be their subordinate.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you think what was going on at the Petkovci school was under the control of somebody from higher command?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as the officers from the higher command came and we hadn't been informed about that, we had not received any orders from my command, I suppose that they had the supreme authority and that they held all the responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I think you may have answered this but I'll clear it up just in case you haven't: Did you have a line of direct communication with, for example, the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not have a line of communication with the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And it may sound a stupid question in the light of that but I assume that's equally true of the Main Staff of the VRS, is it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So if somebody wanted to pass a message or deliver a task to an officer from the Drina Corps or the Main Staff of the VRS and he happened to be in your area, how would they have to do that?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either directly, by telephone, or -- I don't know how else. From my post, nobody ever spoke to any higher command or the Drina Corps or the General Staff and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, was another option to pass a message through brigade command at Standard?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the two communications received on the 14th of July, did either of them have the force of orders or were they just messages?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were messages.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to move on, please, to the vehicle logs, and I hope we can clear this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have in e-court, please, first of all, P945? And we'll need the next page, please. Sorry, this is my mistake. I wanted to start with P944, so can we go back to that? And I think it will be the third page of this document. Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've seen this document before. This is the document that relates to the vehicle that's shown as going to Srebrenica on the 15th of July. It's right, isn't it, that you provided a number of men to take part in the assault force on Srebrenica, Tactical Group 1?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I think it's equally right that two of those men were killed in action and one went missing?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you tell us the name of the man who went missing?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay. But in any event, I think you were asked by his brother whether he could go to Srebrenica on the 15th of July to look for him; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And who went with the man's brother?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vlado Josic drove, and two other men went with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And in relation to that, was it this vehicle that we see on this log that they took?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you know that they were gone for a period of 24 hours or more; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They departed Petkovci at 8.00, and I didn't know when they would return or how long they would stay in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That was your state of knowledge before they went, but you know now that they did go and they were gone for a day or more; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They left on the 15th and they returned on the 16th, they returned to Petkovci on the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So in relation to the vehicle records that we see here, any suggestion that this vehicle might have been used to go to Brana on the 15th is just simply inaccurate, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that yesterday as well, and to the investigators when they asked me, that this seemed illogical to me, that a vehicle should go at 8.00 to Srebrenica, return at 10.00. It's undoable. So I cannot see how this could be possible, Petkovci-Brana-Petkovci on the 15th of July. It's illogical and it sounds impossible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's also right, isn't it, that when you were spoken to by the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor, you were perfectly happy to tell them everything you knew about the two men who might have driven this vehicle?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I explained to them that Vlado Josic volunteered to go, since we had no driver at the moment and there were quite a few problems, namely there were many Muslim soldiers around. It was not free territory yet. So he volunteered to do a favour to the brother of the deceased. It turned out later that the man was deceased, killed somewhere in the area of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Does Vlado Josic still live in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you tell the investigators from the Office of the Prosecutor that and where he could be found?

utterances.speaker: OSTOJA STANISIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He lives in Kozluk, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
